title: Thermal dissipation inspection
body: Thermal heat dissipation: low process-to-air temperature difference and low rotational speed may indicate inadequate heat removal. Review cooling airflow, ventilation and temperature sensor readings. Ask an authorized technician to inspect the cooling system. Follow the site's isolation and lockout procedure before maintenance. This is illustrative guidance, not a manufacturer-approved procedure.

title: Torque and power review
body: Torque load power: unusually high torque or rotational speed can indicate overload or unusual operating conditions. Compare torque and speed with the approved operating envelope. Inspect for obstruction through the site's approved procedure. Escalate to the shift supervisor before changing operating parameters. No automatic machine actuation is permitted.

title: Tool wear inspection
body: Tool wear and overstrain: accumulated tool wear under high torque can indicate increased failure risk. Review tool wear minutes, product type and torque together. Plan an authorized tool inspection, verify replacement availability and record the work order. Use site isolation procedures. Do not infer remaining useful life from this classifier.

title: Telemetry quality and incident triage
body: Missing stale invalid sensor telemetry: check the event timestamp, sensor units, duplicates and source connection before diagnosing a machine fault. Compare the current reading with recent history. Invalid data must be rejected. An unavailable model or disconnected stream should be shown explicitly to the operator.

title: Human approval and escalation
body: Maintenance work order approval: an analyst may draft a recommendation with evidence. A supervisor reviews the evidence and approves or rejects the proposal. Record the decision and audit timestamp. Approval only records a planning decision; it never sends commands to physical equipment. Financial savings require a measured client baseline.
